why: Known debt for the unit-tests step's no-network rule (.github/workflows/pre-merge.yml): each test file, or module, and the hosts it reached with the network refused, measured 2026-09-14. scripts/no_network_verdict.py fails the step on any (file, host) not listed here. Do not add an entry to make a new test pass: stub the fetch. Remove an entry when its file is fixed; retire one that merely went quiet only after every run compared (at least three) was quiet. Retired 2026-09-19: the three images.unsplash.com entries (test_card_brand_tokens, test_grid_inventory_card, test_og_card_fonts). routes/og_cards._library_bg is stubbed by tests/_og_photo_stub.py, so the fetch is gone by construction rather than merely quiet; three runs confirmed it. With the entries gone the gate is armed again for those files — a re-introduced fetch now fails the step instead of passing as registered debt. Retired 2026-09-19: ai_surface_canon.py, the one MODULE entry. The hook attributes to a module only when PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST is unset — a fetch with no test running — and both ways that could happen are closed: module scope does nothing but read two env vars, compile a regex and make two locks, and the file's only two threads (_refresh_public_floors, _refresh_server_version) are the exact pair tests/conftest.py neuters off the main thread. A main-thread call is attributed to the test that makes it. Structural, not merely quiet — and quiet too, across a full local run and the CI verdicts on main and #4789.
